subject: Chemistry

sections.title: Section B - Data and experimental skills

stem: Lake Arda is a below-sea-level hypersaline lake. Its level and ionic composition have been monitored while geothermal extraction and evaporation continue.

parts.label: a
parts.html: (i) Explain why the recorded lake levels are negative.

parts.label: a
parts.html: (ii) Describe how the rate of level change varies from 2000 to 2025, using gradient evidence.

parts.label: a
parts.html: (iii) The average surface area from 2000 to 2010 was 640 km2. Estimate the volume lost over this period in m3.

parts.label: b
parts.html: (i) Suggest two reasons, other than random error, why Survey A and Survey B report different ion concentrations.

parts.label: b
parts.html: (ii) Calculate the percentage increase in Mg2+ from Survey A to Survey B.

parts.label: b
parts.html: (iii) Using Survey A, calculate the molar concentration of Mg2+. Mr(Mg)=24.3.

parts.label: c
parts.html: (i) State the independent and dependent variables in the conductivity investigation.

parts.label: c
parts.html: (ii) State two controlled variables, apart from temperature.

parts.label: c
parts.html: (iii) Calculate the fractional uncertainty in the current at 2.0 m.

parts.label: c
parts.html: (iv) State a conclusion supported by the data and give a chemical explanation.

parts.label: d
parts.html: Describe how a calibration curve could be constructed to determine Mg2+ concentration by spectrophotometry.

questions.title: A hypersaline geothermal lake

solparts.label: a
solparts.html: (i) [1] The reference is mean sea level and the lake surface lies below it.

solparts.label: a
solparts.html: (ii) [2] The level falls throughout and the decline accelerates: the drop is 0.6 m from 2000-2005 but 2.2 m from 2020-2025, so the gradient becomes more negative.

solparts.label: a
solparts.html: (iii) [2] Level drop=1.5 m. Area=640x10^6 m2. Volume=9.60x10^8 m3.

solparts.label: b
solparts.html: (i) [2] Samples may have been collected at different times, depths or locations; evaporation/rainfall/extraction may change concentration; different validated methods or reporting bases may be used.

solparts.label: c
solparts.html: (i) [2] Independent: sampling depth. Dependent: current/conductivity reading.

solparts.label: c
solparts.html: (ii) [2] Electrode separation/area/immersion depth, applied voltage, sample volume, electrode material, calibration and cleaning procedure.

solparts.label: c
solparts.html: (iv) [2] Current increases with depth, indicating higher conductivity. Greater concentration of mobile ions at depth gives more charge carriers.

solparts.label: d
solparts.html: Prepare standards of known concentration; measure absorbance under constant conditions using a blank; plot absorbance against concentration and use the best-fit line to interpolate the sample concentration.

stem: A student heats propan-1-ol under reflux with excess acidified potassium manganate(VII) to prepare propanoic acid. The product is purified and analysed by titration.

parts.label: a
parts.html: Outline two features that favour propanoic acid rather than propanal as the major organic product.

parts.label: b
parts.html: State two safety precautions besides lab coat and goggles.

parts.label: c
parts.html: Explain why titrating the unpurified reaction mixture directly with NaOH would not give a valid propanoic-acid yield.

parts.label: d
parts.html: (i) State two possible impurities removed or separated during purification.

parts.label: d
parts.html: (ii) Explain why collecting a wet distillate and using its total mass as propanoic acid would overestimate yield.

parts.label: e
parts.html: (i) Three 10.00 cm3 samples of a 50.0 cm3 product solution are titrated with 0.200 mol dm-3 NaOH. Use the concordant titres to determine the amount of propanoic acid in the full solution.

parts.label: e
parts.html: (ii) The student began with 1.80 g propan-1-ol. Calculate the percentage yield. Mr(propan-1-ol)=60.1; Mr(propanoic acid)=74.1.

parts.label: f
parts.html: State one reason, apart from incomplete reaction, why the yield may be below 100%.

questions.title: Oxidation of propan-1-ol

solparts.label: a
solparts.html: Use excess oxidizing agent and heat under reflux so volatile aldehyde returns to the reaction flask and is further oxidized.

solparts.label: b
solparts.html: Use a fume hood; avoid flames/use electric heating because alcohol is flammable; wear suitable gloves for corrosive acid/oxidant; clamp glassware and allow cooling before dismantling.

solparts.label: c
solparts.html: Residual sulfuric acid and other acidic species also react with NaOH, causing the titre and calculated propanoic-acid amount to be too high.

solparts.label: d
solparts.html: (i) [1] Water, unreacted propan-1-ol, sulfuric acid, manganese salts or residual oxidant (any two).

solparts.label: d
solparts.html: (ii) [1] The measured mass includes water/other impurities as well as propanoic acid.

solparts.label: e
solparts.html: (i) [4] Mean titre=19.60 cm3. n(NaOH)=0.200x0.01960=0.003920 mol. Reaction is 1:1, so the 10.00 cm3 aliquot contains 0.003920 mol acid. Full 50.0 cm3 contains 0.0196 mol.

solparts.label: e
solparts.html: (ii) [3] Initial alcohol=1.80/60.1=0.02995 mol, theoretical acid=0.02995 mol. Percentage yield=0.0196/0.02995x100=65.4%.

solparts.label: f
solparts.html: Product lost during transfer/distillation, side reactions, incomplete separation, product remaining in apparatus, or sampling/titration uncertainty with a valid link.

instructions: Answer every structured question. Show working, use units and significant figures appropriately, and support conclusions with evidence from the supplied data.
